criteria.text: `poolConfig(url)` for a local host (`localhost` or `127.0.0.1`) returns `ssl: undefined`, with or without `PG_SSL_CA` set — unchanged from today.
`poolConfig(url)` strips `sslmode` from the connection string in both the local and the non-local case (regression check on existing behavior).
`poolConfig(url)` for a non-local host with `PG_SSL_CA` set returns `ssl.rejectUnauthorized === true` and `ssl.ca` equal to the exact string read from `PG_SSL_CA` (no transform applied).
`poolConfig(url)` for a non-local host with `PG_SSL_CA` unset throws synchronously, and the thrown error's message contains the literal string `PG_SSL_CA`.
None of the above is checked by opening a real connection: the tests call `poolConfig` directly and never construct a `pg.Pool` or a `PGlite` instance.

Importing `src/db.ts` under the existing test environment (`DATA_DIR=memory://`, `DATABASE_URL` and `POSTGRES_URL` both unset) does not throw, regardless of whether `PG_SSL_CA` is set — the whole `pnpm test` suite keeps working unmodified.
`src/push.ts` has no `ssl:` key of its own in its pool construction — verified by reading the file — so it inherits criteria 1–4 through the same exported `poolConfig` with no separate change.

The docs state, as a fact findable across the reference pages, that a non-local database connection requires `PG_SSL_CA` (the Postgres server's CA certificate, PEM text) and that a missing value stops the connection rather than falling back to an unverified one. Checked against `docsText` in `test/docs.ts`, not against one page's wording or heading.

The docs state, as a fact, that `PG_SSL_CA` must be set in the deploy target (Vercel) before a deploy that talks to a non-local database, alongside the existing `DATABASE_URL`/`POSTGRES_URL` mention. Checked against `docsText`, not against one page's wording.

`.github/workflows/ingest.yml` passes a `PG_SSL_CA` value from a repository secret into the `ingest` job's environment, alongside `DATABASE_URL` — checked by reading the workflow file. Without this, the scheduled ingest job (which connects to the non-local production database) starts failing closed the moment this change merges, which is a regression this issue must not introduce silently.

The comment immediately above `poolConfig` in `src/db.ts` no longer states or implies that a non-local connection is unverified; it describes the CA-verification behavior instead.

Criterion 8 and 9 are new facts, not covered by `test/docs-drift.test.ts`: that suite only checks the collector/source table (`docs/sources.md` rows against `collectors`/`defaultSources`), which has nothing to do with database TLS configuration. No new criterion duplicates it.
